title: Telegram allowlist default and AND/OR semantics

options.name: Keep current behaviour: empty list means allow, and sender OR channel is enough
options.risk: With no lists (the default), or with only one list set, every message the account can see is accepted, so anyone posting in any visible chat can push a token into the buy pipeline (the safety gates still run).

options.name: Fail closed by default (no lists = Telegram intake off) and require both lists when both are set (AND)
options.behavior_impact: Only messages from an allowed sender in an allowed chat are used.
options.risk: A trusted source posting from a new chat is ignored until configured.

options.name: Fail closed by default and add an explicit mode setting (sender, channel, both, either)
options.behavior_impact: Semantics are stated in config instead of implied by which lists are empty.
options.risk: One more setting to get right; a wrong mode is still possible but visible.

options.name: Fail closed and allow by sender only (channels ignored)
options.behavior_impact: Trust follows people, wherever they post.
options.risk: A compromised or impersonated sender account is trusted in any chat.

recommendation: Fail closed by default with explicit semantics (research recommendation): fail-closed-explicit-mode, or fail-closed-and if a single fixed rule is preferred.
default: Keep current behaviour until the owning phase decides (milestone contract). This card covers S0/S1 capital findings, which cannot rest on the default: until it is decided and fixed it blocks the live re-entry gate.
behavior_impact: Decides which Telegram messages can trigger a buy.
needed_by: Phase 24 discussion (capital fixes, after the Phase 23 real-path proof)
